subject: business-studies
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: A trade-off between ethics and profit occurs when:
options: Ethics and profit always rise together
Doing the most ethical thing reduces profit, forcing a choice
questions.explain: A trade-off means choosing the more ethical option may lower profit, so the business must balance the two.

questions.q: Consumer protection law mainly exists to:
options: Ensure goods are safe, as described and of satisfactory quality
Set the prices of all goods
questions.explain: Consumer law protects buyers by requiring goods to be safe, as described and of satisfactory quality.

options: A general rise in the price level over time
A fall in the number of workers
A rise in interest rates only
questions.explain: Inflation is a sustained increase in the general level of prices in an economy.

questions.q: If interest rates rise, what is a likely effect on businesses?
options: The cost of borrowing increases, which can reduce investment and consumer spending
questions.explain: Higher interest rates raise borrowing costs and can reduce both business investment and consumer spending.

questions.q: Reducing a business's environmental impact might involve:
options: Recycling, cutting waste and using renewable energy
questions.explain: Businesses reduce environmental impact through recycling, cutting waste and using cleaner energy.

options: Minimum wage, discrimination and working conditions
questions.explain: Employment law covers areas such as the minimum wage, anti-discrimination and safe working conditions.

questions.q: How can new technology act as an external influence on a business?
options: It can create new products and ways of selling but requires investment
It always lowers all costs immediately
It removes the need for any staff
It never changes how businesses operate
questions.explain: Technology creates new products and selling methods but often needs investment and training to adopt.

questions.q: An increase in competition is likely to:
options: Put pressure on a business to lower prices or improve quality
Have no effect on the business
Always remove the need to advertise
questions.explain: More competition pressures businesses to compete on price, quality or service to keep customers.

questions.q: High unemployment in the economy is likely to mean:
options: Consumers have more money to spend
Lower consumer incomes and reduced demand for many products
questions.explain: High unemployment lowers overall incomes and tends to reduce demand for many goods and services.

questions.q: A possible benefit to a business of international trade is:
options: No need to consider exchange rates
Access to larger markets and more customers abroad
questions.explain: International trade gives businesses access to larger markets and new customers overseas.

questions.q: Globalisation has made it easier for businesses to:
options: Trade and operate across international borders
questions.explain: Globalisation has increased trade and the ability of firms to operate across countries.

questions.q: During a recession (a downturn in the business cycle), businesses often experience:
questions.explain: In a recession consumer spending falls, so many businesses see lower demand and sales.
